title: O, Who Shall See the Glorious Day
description: O, Who Shall See the Glorious Day in Tonic Solfa to ALL SAINTS, NEW, doh is Bb: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 2 verses and a piano.
about: Thomas Moore wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 316 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “The Same”.

The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre Double (8.6.8.6.8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ALL SAINTS, NEW; any other Common Metre Double tune fits them as well.
underlay: O, who shall see the glo-rious day, When, throned on Zi-on's brow, The Lord shall rend the veil a-way That hides the na-tions now! When earth no more be-neath the fear Of his re-buke shall lie, When pain shall cease, and ev-ery tear Be wiped from ev-ery eye!

lines: O, who shall see the glorious day,
The Lord shall rend the veil away
When earth no more beneath the fear
When pain shall cease, and every tear
Then, Judah, thou no more shalt mourn
Thy days of splendor shall return,
The fount of life shall then be quaffed
In peace by all who come;
And every wind that blows, shall waft

licence: Public domain: Thomas Moore died in 1852.
credits: Words by Thomas Moore (1779–1852), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to ALL SAINTS, NEW by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
